title: Loop+ Membership Household Sharing Rules
content:
The owner of a Loop+ Membership may share some benefits with the members of a household, within the numbers the owner's plan allows.

**Rule.** The owner may share benefits with up to the plan's household adults and household teens; a plan allowing zero shares nothing. Shopping benefits used by a household adult or teen are recorded on the owner's membership and count as benefit uses of that membership for refund purposes. Music is shared only on the family music tier; video, photo storage and deal early access belong to the owner and adults only. Removing a household member never changes the owner's fee.

## Who may use what

| Benefit | Owner | Household adult | Household teen |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shopping benefits | yes | yes, recorded on the owner's membership | yes, recorded on the owner's membership |
| Loop+ Video | yes | yes | no |
| Unlimited photo storage | yes | yes | no |
| Lightning Deal early access | yes | yes | no |
| Loop+ Music | yes | shared only on the family music tier | shared only on the family music tier |

The household columns apply only up to the number of household adults and household teens the plan allows. Where a plan allows zero of either, nothing is shared with that kind of household member.

## Points of judgement

- **Recording.** A shopping benefit used by a household adult or teen is a benefit use of the owner's membership: it is recorded there and counts for refund purposes exactly as the owner's own use does.
- **Music.** On the individual music tier, Loop+ Music is not shared; it is shared only on the family music tier.
- **Fee.** Removing a household member never changes the owner's fee.

## Hypothetical case

An owner's plan allows 1 household adult and 0 teens. The owner adds one adult, who places an order using free shipping. That use is recorded on the owner's membership and counts as a benefit use of it for refund purposes. The adult may also watch Loop+ Video. No teen can be added, because the plan allows zero.
